patient.chief_complaint: Right-sided weakness and facial droop — 5 days after extreme stress event
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. C is a 33-year-old freelance artist and single mother who presents with right-sided arm and leg weakness and right facial droop of 5 days duration. She received an eviction notice 4 weeks ago and is in a financial crisis, with no family support system. The neurological symptoms began abruptly approximately 5 days ago during a particularly stressful confrontation with her landlord. She reports the right-side weakness came on rapidly within minutes of the confrontation. She denies any headache at onset. She is on an oral contraceptive pill for contraception. The combination of young female, OCP use, and acute-onset hemiparesis requires exclusion of OCP-associated thrombotic stroke or cerebral venous thrombosis. She denies any progressive headache, papilledema symptoms, or visual changes. She has no prior neurological presentations. Her facial droop is inconsistent during examination — present when formally asked to smile, absent during spontaneous conversation. She is resistant to any psychological explanation, stating she has real weakness and needs a medical diagnosis to qualify for housing assistance.

key_reasoning_points: OCP use in a young woman with acute hemiparesis REQUIRES MR venography to exclude cerebral venous thrombosis — CVT risk is 6x higher with OCP use
Protein S is physiologically reduced by OCPs — mildly low result should not be attributed to inherited protein S deficiency without confirming off OCP

Facial droop that disappears spontaneously (present on formal exam, absent during spontaneous facial movement) is a specific positive functional sign — organic facial palsies are consistent regardless of context
Social determinants of health (housing crisis, social isolation) must be addressed in parallel with FND treatment — failure to address social crisis predicts treatment failure
